messages:
Alex (Support): Customer reports repeated 401s and says they can't find any request/trace id in their HAR. Time window: 2026-03-16 14:03-14:07 UTC. They attached a partial HAR but no x-redwood-* headers visible. Any quick triage steps?

Priya (SRE): First ask for the full HAR + exact endpoint path (e.g. /v1/generate or /v1/embeddings) and the client auth header they used. If headers were stripped by a proxy you won't see x-redwood-request-id. Quick checklist: 
- Confirm Authorization header used in request
- Search HAR for "x-redwood-request-id" or "x-redwood-trace-id" (case-insensitive)
- If absent, check for any upstream proxy that may remove custom headers (ask for proxy config)

Alex (Support): They said mobile webview (embedded) + a CDN in front. What's the best ask for a minimal repro?

Priya (SRE): Ask customer to repro with a direct curl from a workstation (no CDN) so we can get a clear request. Provide this curl snippet: 

```bash
curl -i \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate\" \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <their_api_key>' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

Then ask them to paste the response headers exactly. If we see a 401 and response body like {"error":"invalid_api_key"} that's useful. If the curl works (200) but the webview fails, that strongly points at the CDN or webview stripping headers.

Mike (Eng): If they can share the HAR, tell them where to look in the UI: Console -> Requests -> filter by time range -> click an entry -> "Headers" tab shows request headers including x-redwood-request-id and x-redwood-trace-id. If they don't have console access, request a HAR and we can search for request.url matching /v1/ and then inspect request.headers in the HAR JSON.

Alex (Support): For mobile SDKs any quick captures?

Priya (SRE): Android: enable SDK debug logs `RedwoodSdk.setLogLevel(LogLevel.DEBUG)` and capture logcat around the request time. iOS: set Redwood logging to verbose. Both SDKs log the outbound headers and will include the request id header when the server returns it. Also request they toggle the SDK flag that includes internal debug header (if enabled on their account) — e.g., `X-Redwood-Debug: 1` so server includes debug metadata in response.

Alex (Support): If they can't share a HAR, can we still get something?

Mike (Eng): Yes — ask for: 
- Exact UTC time window (to the minute)
- The client IP or approximate region
- The full Authorization header mask (first 6 chars ok)
- A minimal repro curl above

If they can run a quick curl and show us response headers we often get `x-redwood-request-id: ab12cd34` which maps into our trace system. Then we can pull the full trace.

Priya (SRE): If they created a console debug bundle (Console -> Support -> Create debug bundle) ask them to paste the debug token. We can then attach server-side logs and the exact request trace. Example flow in message to customer: 

"Please re-run the failing request with a curl (example attached), upload a HAR or paste the response headers, and if possible create a debug bundle from the Console and paste the token here. If you can't access the Console, send the HAR and the exact UTC minute window and we'll search logs."

Alex (Support): If headers are completely missing due to proxy rewrite, what's the escalation path?

Mike (Eng): Escalate to Networking / Customer infra: ask for a packet capture or proxy policy showing header whitelist. Also ask customer to add a temporary passthrough rule for the api.redwood.com host. If they can't change proxy, we can suggest adding a custom query param `?rwd_trace=1` as a temporary last-resort signal (but prefer preserved headers).

debug-bot: :thumbsup: flagged for follow-up if debug token created.

Alex (Support): I'll send the curl + debug bundle steps to the customer and request the exact minute range. Will post back when they reply. Thanks all. :pray:
